extraction.name: Visual Genome
extraction.description: Visual Genome is a dataset to enable the modeling of relationships between objects in images. It contains dense annotations of objects, attributes, and relationships within each image. The dataset contains over 100K images where each image has an average of 21 objects, 18 attributes, and 18 pairwise relationships between objects. Objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases in region descriptions and question answer pairs are canonicalized to WordNet synsets.
extraction.creator: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bernstein, Li Fei-Fei
extraction.citeAs: Ranjay Krishna et al. Visual Genome: Connecting Language and Vision Using Crowdsourced Dense Image Annotations. arXiv:1602.07332v1 [cs.CV] 23 Feb 2016
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Visual Genome was collected entirely by crowd workers from Amazon Mechanical Turk. The dataset was collected over the course of 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation. Approximately 800,000 Human Intelligence Tasks (HITs) were launched on AMT. Overall, a total of over 33,000 unique workers contributed to the dataset. Each HIT was designed such that workers manage to earn anywhere between $6-$8 per hour if they work continuously. Visual Genome HITs achieved a 94.1% retention rate.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The Visual Genome dataset uses 108,249 images from the intersection of the YFCC100M and MS-COCO datasets. These images are real-world, non-iconic images that were uploaded onto Flickr by users.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The dataset was collected over the course of 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For region descriptions: lowercase, lemmatize, and strip excess whitespace from all attributes. BLEU score thresholds set to 0.7 to ensure descriptions are dissimilar to previously written descriptions. For objects: Stanford's dependency parser was used to extract nouns automatically. For attributes: normalize each attribute based on morphology (stemming) and map them to WordNet adjectives. For relationships: ignore all prepositions as they are not recognized by WordNet. All components undergo canonicalization to WordNet synsets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Region descriptions: Workers draw bounding boxes and write descriptions for regions. Process repeated until 50 region descriptions collected per image. Workers explicitly encouraged to write descriptions that have not been written before. Objects: Extracted from region descriptions by crowd workers who draw bounding boxes around each object. Attributes and Relationships: Workers add attributes to objects or connect pairs of objects with relationships based on region description text. Question Answers: Workers write pairs of questions and answers about images following three rules: start with one of the seven Ws, avoid ambiguous questions, be precise and unique.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All Visual Genome data go through a verification stage using two strategies: majority voting (three unique workers vote on whether annotation is factually correct, annotation added if at least two verify it is correct) and rapid judgments (used specifically for verifying objects with an order of magnitude increase in speed).
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Each image contains an average of 42 region descriptions, 21 objects, 16 attributes, 18 relationships, and 17 question-answer pairs.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 93.02% of workers contributed from the United States. The majority of workers were between the ages of 25 and 34 years old. The youngest contributor was 18 years old and the oldest was 68 years old. 54.15% male and 45.85% female workers. Workers also contributed from Philippines (1.29%), Kenya (1.13%), India (0.94%), Russia (0.50%), Canada (0.47%), and other countries (2.65%).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford NLP tools (Manning et al., 2014) were used to extract noun phrases from region descriptions and QAs, and to extract nouns automatically to speed up object extraction process. VGG 16-layer network (Simonyan and Zisserman, 2014) was used for feature extraction in experiments.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Our dataset is somewhat biased towards images of people. The images range from as small as 72 pixels wide to as large as 1280 pixels wide, with an average width of 500 pixels. The top synsets show bias towards sports-related images (ski, ballplayer, racket). Certain sports (skiing, surfboarding) are overrepresented due to a bias towards these sports in the images.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The canonicalization mappings are not perfect and still contain some ambiguity. For relationship classification, accuracy results are much lower than attribute prediction because of the high intra-class variability of most relationships. Current models are unable to reason about complex images, as illustrated by objectively low accuracy in region description generation experiments. The attribute clique graphs and relationship prediction experiments show that some attributes and relationships occur exclusively with a small number of objects.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation. The dataset enables modeling of relationships between objects in images for cognitive computer vision tasks including: dense image captioning, visual question answering, image understanding evaluation, relationship extraction, semantic image retrieval, attribute prediction, and relationship prediction. The dataset can be used to train models that understand interactions and relationships between objects in images.
